rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nepal: 10 national parks, 6 conservation areas, 1 hunting reserve, Ramsar wetlands.  ·  Chitwan (1973): first park; Bengal tiger + one-horned rhino; UNESCO World Heritage.  ·  Sagarmatha (1976): Everest; UNESCO World Heritage.  ·  IUCN: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Chitwan National Park (1985) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the first Nepali park.  ·  The one-horned rhino (Rhinoceros unicornis) is found ONLY in Nepal and India.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Detailed notes on 02 national parks wildlife reserves conservation areas biodiversity hotspots wetland and ramsar sites wildlife importance causes of extinction and conservation strategies iucn categories of threatened species endangered species in nepal within the conservation biology unit.  ·  Protected areas: designated areas for conservation; in Nepal: 10 national parks, 6 conservation areas, 1 hunting reserve, and Ramsar wetlands.  ·  National parks: Chitwan (1973, Bengal tiger + one-horned rhino), Bardia, Banke, Shuklaphanta, Koshi Tappu, Parsa, Rara, Langtang (1976), Sagarmatha (1976), Annapurna (1986), Manaslu (1986), Makalu (1992), Kanchenjunga (1989). NEB commonly cites 10 national parks; several sources list 11–14 depending on inclusion of the newer parks.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Biodiversity conservation involves safeguarding and scientifically managing diverse life forms to sustain their levels and provide lasting benefits for current and future generations.  ·  It protects plant, animal, microbial, and genetic resources crucial for food production, agriculture, and ecosystem functions like soil fertilization, nutrient recycling, pest control, erosion prevention, and crop and tree pollination.  ·  Conservation practices aim to manage nature and resources for present and future generations, ensuring the sustained well-being of humanity.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: There are two basic strategies of biodiversity conservation: a.  ·  In-Situ Conservation (within natural habitat): This method protects organisms in their natural habitats like national parks and other protected areas.  ·  Endangered in Nepal: tiger (EN), rhino (VU), snow leopard (VU), elephant (EN), red panda (VU).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Causes of extinction: habitat loss, poaching, pollution, climate change, invasive species.  ·  Strategies: in-situ, ex-situ, community forestry, anti-poaching, CITES, awareness.  ·  • National parks
